entities.summary: Dōkyō was a Japanese monk who rose to power through the favor of Empress Kōken and became a Daijō-daijin Zenji, the rank set up for him, and later became a Hōō, the highest rank of the religious world. Born in Wakae district in 700 CE, Dōkyō played a crucial role in shaping the religious and political landscape of medieval Japan. He was instrumental in the development of the Shingon school of Buddhism, which emphasized the attainment of enlightenment through ritual and meditation. Dōkyō's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he paved the way for the rise of Zen Buddhism in Japan. His influence can be seen in the many temples and shrines he founded, which continue to be revered today. Dōkyō's life was marked by controversy, as he was accused of heresy and later stripped of his titles. Despite this, he remains one of the most important figures in Japanese religious history.
